scope: flash-v7-20260927-01 cases 01..24; after case-finish, independently read each own request, visible raw, parsed first/repair and final product.
major_findings: 03/12/18/21/24 first answers give an insufficient ledger but empty issues. All five repairs create cited Issues; only 03 also meets the frozen category requirement. Correct basis alone is not accepted delivery.
06 still excuses unsupported record attribution as reported content/no_issue: this is a substantive semantic omission.

09/12/15/18/19/21/24 retain category failures. 13 reverses direct-fact/context-premise roles. 10 and 15 include undeclared optional context under the unchanged scoring policy; these are distinct from core reasoning being wrong.

22 correctly identifies the west/east contradiction but cites SourceSpan4 known only through Memory; allowed evidence is 5/1/2. The unbound citation causes terminal evidence_unresolvable, not an invented location fact.
21 no longer calls the complete input truncated, but still paraphrases away the grinding-agent predicate and misclassifies the repair as character_knowledge rather than relationship.
01/13 final products strip timeless-rule suggestions and apply_suggestion under existing behavior; 01 remains accepted, 13 retains its evidence-role failures.
limitations: Seen development inputs and one rerun cannot establish general model capability or isolate causal improvement. The fixed V6 categories, minimum/optional sources and roles are unchanged.
V6 historical results are read, not rescored or edited. V5 record-attribution ambiguity remains disclosed; V7 uses the predeclared story-fact P scope for 15/24.
15 explanation says 'opposite' while reasoning explicitly preserves unknown birth order; this is imprecise attribution wording, not proof of reverse birth order.
Each real request matches independently accepted preparation content. Product legacy revision-display field semantics do not replace runtime/request binding.

First product-contract pass is structural/temporal, not full accuracy; terminal output is never no-conflict. No reviewer Provider calls, database connections, runner execution, product edits or historical rescoring.
